risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: The function receives an open AsyncConnection and never commits/rolls back the outer transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The caller owns the transaction; row locks (FOR UPDATE) and the dependent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

architectural_decisions.decision: The whole procedure body (validations included) runs inside `async with conn.begin_nested():`; the WHEN OTHERS handler runs after the savepoint context exits, inserts the error audit row, and re-raises.
architectural_decisions.rationale: In PL/pgSQL the EXCEPTION clause covers the entire block, so validation RAISEs also trigger the audit insert; the savepoint rollback keeps the transaction usable for the handler's INSERT, exactly like the original.

architectural_decisions.decision: All SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, UPDATE and INSERT statements remain parameterized SQL via sqlalchemy.text().
architectural_decisions.rationale: Locking and DML belong close to the database; Python only coordinates validation and control flow.

architectural_decisions.decision: Each RAISE EXCEPTION message maps to a dedicated exception subclass of TransferenciaError; the handler logs via logging and re-raises the original exception.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Preserves the original error surface while giving callers typed exceptions; SQLERRM is approximated by the exception message (or its asyncpg .orig).

warnings: SQLERRM is approximated by str(exception) (preferring the driver's .orig when present); the exact PostgreSQL error text may differ slightly.
The error-audit INSERT in the handler can itself fail (e.g. connection lost); in PL/pgSQL that failure would also abort the procedure — behaviour is equivalent.
The success-path logger.info call has no direct PL/pgSQL counterpart (the original emits no NOTICE); it is informational only and can be removed.
p_valor is expected as decimal.Decimal (NUMERIC(18,2)); passing float would change precision semantics.
The helper _unused_type_guard exists only to keep the Any import referenced; it can be deleted together with the import if desired.
